sections.title: World
sections.gist: Israel's election ended in deadlock, with Netanyahu and challenger Gadi Eisenkot both racing to build the next coalition.

items.headline: Israel's election leaves a hung Knesset, coalition talks begin
items.what: Israel voted on **October 27**, and neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot won the **61 seats** needed to govern. Both claim they can form the next government. Up to **480,000** ballots from soldiers, police and diplomats are still being counted, so the final seat count could still shift.
items.why_it_matters: A drawn-out coalition fight leaves Israel without clear leadership while it manages a fragile Gaza ceasefire and tension with Iran.
items.context: No Israeli party has ever won a majority alone, so the winner must build a coalition from smaller parties. President Isaac Herzog, whose office denied floating a unity deal, could end up picking who gets first shot at forming a government.
items.next: Final results, including overseas and military ballots, may take **days** to confirm.
items.insight: A hung result could make whoever governs dependent on small kingmaker parties — the same dynamic that strained Netanyahu's last coalition.

terms.meaning: Israel's 120-seat parliament; a party or bloc needs 61 seats to form a government.

sections.title: India
sections.gist: Delhi-NCR's winter pollution plan kicks in from November 1, with vehicle bans, work-from-home rules and construction curbs tightening by stage.

items.headline: Delhi's winter pollution curbs kick in from November 1
items.what: Delhi's air quality regulator already triggered **Stage I** curbs on **October 21** as smog returned. From **November 1**, the city bans non-BS-VI petrol and diesel vehicles from outside Delhi, and government offices start **50% work-from-home**. Outdoor construction and demolition face a full ban from **December 10** to **January 20**.
items.why_it_matters: Anyone in Delhi-NCR will feel this: more WFH days, costlier parking, and tighter checks on fuel and older vehicles.
items.context: CAQM, the government body that manages Delhi-NCR's smog response, tightened its **Graded Response Action Plan** on **September 28**. The plan ranks restrictions by how bad the air gets, and this year adds fixed calendar dates instead of waiting for pollution to spike first.
items.next: Expect **Stage II or III** curbs — tighter vehicle and construction bans — if AQI keeps climbing into November.
items.insight: Fixed calendar dates, rather than reacting to AQI spikes, suggest authorities are betting prevention beats emergency response — a shift after years of criticism that GRAP kicks in too late.

terms.meaning: Graded Response Action Plan — rules that tighten automatically as Delhi's air gets worse.

sections.title: Affects you
sections.gist: Cyclone Arnab forced mass evacuations and school closures on the Andhra-Odisha coast, while the delayed UPI merchant fee still has no new start date.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab floods Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts
items.what: **Cyclone Arnab** crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast around **October 28**. Around **89,000 people** were evacuated in the Kakinada region to 101 relief camps, and over **8,000 more** moved to safety in Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued red and orange alerts for heavy rain and strong winds.
items.why_it_matters: Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres shut in affected Odisha districts, and heavy rain is forecast to keep falling into other states through **October 30**.
items.context: Cyclones form over the warm Bay of Bengal in October-November and can bring destructive winds and flooding to India's east coast. Storms are named in rotation using names contributed by countries in the region, which is how this one got called Arnab.
items.next: Watch for IMD's confirmation of the exact landfall point and how fast the storm weakens over land.
items.insight: Evacuating nearly 100,000 people before landfall shows India's early-warning system, rebuilt after past cyclones' high death tolls, holding up.

terms.meaning: India Meteorological Department — the government agency that tracks storms and issues weather warnings.

items.headline: UPI merchant fee still has no new start date
items.what: NPCI's **0.4% fee** on UPI payments above ₹2,000 to shops was due to start October 15 but was pushed back for the festive season. No new date has been confirmed; NPCI has only said it will begin **'immediately post-Diwali.'** Diwali falls on **November 8**, so the fee could start within two weeks.
items.why_it_matters: Shops may soon start passing on a small surcharge or asking for cash on bigger bills.
items.context: UPI is the tap-to-pay system behind PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, free to use since 2016. Banks that run it want a cut of the cost on larger payments to shops, while payments between friends and family stay free.
items.next: Watch NPCI's website for the official date, expected right after November 8.

sections.title: Markets & money
sections.gist: Alphabet's stock crashed 10% on an earnings miss despite a cloud boom, and the Fed's split rate hold raised the odds of a December hike.

items.headline: Alphabet's stock drops 10% despite cloud revenue surge
items.what: Alphabet reported quarterly earnings of **$2.12 a share** on October 28, well below the **$3.02** analysts expected. Revenue rose 25% to about **$127 billion**, but still missed forecasts, even as Google Cloud revenue surged **103%** to $30.7 billion. Investors sent the stock down about **10%** in after-hours and early trading.
items.why_it_matters: A nearly **$400 billion** drop in Alphabet's value shows investors losing patience with how much Big Tech spends on AI before it pays off.
items.context: Alphabet is Google's parent company, and Google Cloud rents computing power and AI tools to other businesses. Microsoft, Amazon and Meta are also spending hundreds of billions on AI data centers, and investors are watching closely for proof it pays off.
items.next: Amazon reports its own results on **October 29**, the last of this week's Big Tech earnings.
items.insight: Markets now judge AI spending less on growth and more on cash burn — Alphabet's cloud revenue surged, but the stock fell anyway.

items.headline: Fed holds rates steady, two officials wanted a hike
items.what: The US Federal Reserve left its rate unchanged at **3.75%-4.00%** on October 28, as most traders expected. The vote was **10-2**, with policymakers Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanting a quarter-point hike instead. The Fed's statement called the economy strong but inflation still elevated.
items.why_it_matters: A split vote raises the odds of a hike in December, keeping borrowing costlier for longer worldwide, including for India's rupee and import bills.
items.context: The Fed sets the interest rate that ripples through loans, mortgages and markets worldwide. It last moved in September, raising rates for the first time since 2023.
items.next: Markets now price roughly an **80% chance** of a hike at the next meeting on **December 9**.
items.insight: Two officials openly wanting a hike is unusually hawkish — a sign some policymakers see pausing as riskier than raising rates.

terms.meaning: The Federal Reserve committee that meets roughly every six weeks to set the US interest rate.

sections.title: Tech & AI
sections.gist: Microsoft's cloud grew 48% on AI demand and its stock rose, the one bright spot in a mixed week of Big Tech earnings.

items.headline: Microsoft's cloud jumps 48% as AI demand outruns expectations
items.what: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of **$92.3 billion**, up 19%, beating Wall Street's forecast. Its cloud computing arm Azure grew **48%** to $33.2 billion, the fastest pace in years. Investors sent the stock up in premarket trading after the October 28 report.
items.why_it_matters: Strong Azure demand is the clearest evidence yet that companies are actually paying to use AI, not just investing in it on faith.
items.context: Azure is Microsoft's cloud service, renting computing power that runs other companies' apps and AI models. Microsoft, Google and Amazon are racing to build data centers for AI, spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year.
items.next: Microsoft expects Azure growth to accelerate further next quarter, to **49-50%**, testing if demand keeps outrunning supply.
items.insight: Microsoft breaking out Azure's exact dollar revenue for the first time suggests it wants investors focused on cloud strength, not its slowing core software growth.

sections.title: Science, health & climate
sections.gist: Africa's deadliest Ebola outbreak kept spreading, with confirmed cases now reaching Congo, Kenya and Nigeria.

items.headline: Ebola outbreak in Africa spreads to Kenya and Nigeria
items.what: Congo's Ebola outbreak has infected **over 9,400 people** and killed **more than 4,500** since May, the deadliest in the country's history. It has spread to **eight provinces**, and Kenya has confirmed **nine cases** after a traveler from Congo died in Nairobi on October 5. Nigeria reported its first case on October 20.
items.why_it_matters: A deadly virus with no vaccine has now reached three countries, raising fears it could spread to cities far from the original outbreak.
items.context: The virus is the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, a rarer form first identified in Uganda in 2007. Unlike the more common Ebola Zaire strain, there is no approved vaccine or treatment for it yet.
items.next: Health officials are tracing contacts in Kenya and Nigeria to stop further spread before it reaches more cities.
items.insight: The outbreak has run since May without a vaccine ready, showing how little has changed since West Africa's 2014 Ebola crisis exposed the same gap.

sections.title: Formula 1
sections.gist: Kimi Antonelli, 20, stands one race from becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever champion at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.

items.headline: Antonelli one race from becoming F1's youngest-ever champion
items.what: Kimi Antonelli, 20, won the **US Grand Prix** in Austin from pole, his ninth win this season. He now leads George Russell by **123 points** and Lewis Hamilton by **124**, with just 125 points left this year. A ninth-place finish at Sunday's Mexico City race would clinch the title outright.
items.why_it_matters: A win for Antonelli would make him F1's youngest-ever champion, a changing of the guard after Hamilton and Verstappen's decade of dominance.
items.context: Antonelli, an Italian teenager, replaced seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025 as the youngest driver on the grid. Sebastian Vettel held the youngest-champion record before this, winning his first title at 23 in 2010.
items.next: The Mexico City Grand Prix, where Antonelli can clinch the title, runs Sunday, **November 1**.
items.insight: A rookie topping the title fight in just his second season signals Mercedes' power unit, not just driver talent, now leads the field.

terms.meaning: Starting the race from the front of the grid, having set the fastest qualifying lap.

sections.title: Cricket — the masala
sections.gist: IPL franchises begin reshuffling squads ahead of the 2027 mini-auction, set for December in Goa.

items.headline: IPL's 2027 auction trades begin, mini-auction set for Dec 16
items.what: Delhi Capitals traded fast bowler **T. Natarajan** back to Sunrisers Hyderabad on **October 14**, swapping him for leg-spinner Zeeshan Ansari. Franchises must submit retention lists by **November 15**, ahead of a mini-auction in **Goa on December 16**. It is the first IPL auction held in India since 2022.
items.why_it_matters: Trades like this reshuffle squads months before the auction, and signal which stars franchises are willing to let go.
items.context: The IPL is India's hugely popular T20 cricket league, where eight to ten city franchises bid for players each year. Natarajan had barely played for Delhi since joining in a ₹10.75 crore mega-auction deal in 2025.
items.next: Franchises' retention lists are due **November 15**, setting the player pool for December's auction.
items.insight: Holding the auction in India again, not Dubai, suggests the BCCI wants the spectacle and broadcast revenue back home.
